title: Algorithmic efficiency and scaling
ranking_basis: Controlled inspectable timing first; data-efficiency optimization second; historical model-based coverage third, conditional on rights/access.
interpretation_guards: No universal efficiency curve. A matched target is necessary but insufficient without compatible workload, data, evaluation, resource and accounting regimes.
Optimizer and hyperparameters are treatments, not controls required to be identical.
Checkpoint counts are not trial counts. Absence of an observed crossing is not budget exhaustion or confirmed failure.
Archive, execution-code, experiment, publication and retrieval versions/times remain distinct.
No energy series verified. Hardware identity, nominal power and FLOPs do not establish joules. No efficiency-to-risk or p(doom) conversion.
Public access is not a reuse grant. License scope and full-source versus curated-derivative hashes remain separate.

collections.measurement_regime: Controlled training submission-time-to-target within fixed workload, hardware and tuning protocol.
limitations: One trial is not an official aggregate score, a five-trial search result, a five-study median or a failure-rate estimate. Seventy-four checkpoints are not replicates.
External tuning has five trials per study and five studies; selected best-trial time excludes the total search expenditure. Self-tuning has a different budget regime.
Optimizer and full hyperparameters are treatments. Workload/version, architecture, evaluation target, hardware/resource regime and timing rules are comparison constraints.
Published approximately 28% speedup has failed-run budget substitution and omitted held-out invalidation qualifications; it is not an unconditional compute reduction.
No paired baseline in the pilot: no efficiency ratio, energy estimate, FLOP inference, secular scaling rate or risk probability.
